definitions.explanation: The gradual loss of the eye's ability to focus on nearby objects, typically occurring around age 40 and older.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}、{老眼|ろうがん}で{小|ちい}さい{字|じ}が{読|よ}みにくくなった。
examples.english: Lately, I've had trouble reading small print due to presbyopia.

examples.japanese: 40{歳|さい}を{過|す}ぎると{老眼|ろうがん}が{始|はじ}まることが{多|おお}い。
{老眼鏡|ろうがんきょう}をかけて{新聞|しんぶん}を{読|よ}む。
examples.english: I wear reading glasses to read the newspaper.

notes:
USAGE: {老眼|ろうがん} is a natural age-related condition affecting nearly everyone eventually. It's distinct from other vision problems.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{老眼|ろうがん}になる (to develop presbyopia)
・{老眼|ろうがん}が{進|すす}む (presbyopia progresses)
・{老眼鏡|ろうがんきょう} (reading glasses)
・{老眼|ろうがん}{用|よう}レンズ (lenses for presbyopia)

OTHER VISION CONDITIONS:
・{近視|きんし} - nearsightedness (myopia)
・{遠視|えんし} - farsightedness (hyperopia) - not age-related
・{乱視|らんし} - astigmatism

NOTE ON TERMINOLOGY: {老眼|ろうがん} is sometimes translated as "farsightedness," but technically it's presbyopia (aging-related), while {遠視|えんし} is hyperopia (can occur at any age).
